missing: safety contra 2020 (rat and monkey repeat-dose toxicology): Smith B, Rowe J, Watkins PB, Ashina M, Woodhead JL, Sistare FD (Merck), Goadsby PJ. Mechanistic Investigations Support Liver Safety of Ubrogepant. Toxicol Sci 2020;177(1):84-93, doi 10.1093/toxsci/kfaa093, PMID 32579200, PMC8312697, epub 2020-06-24. Results, verbatim: 'Results from conventional nonclinical animal toxicology studies, each conducted in 2 or more species, did not reveal liver safety liabilities for telcagepant, MK-3207, or ubrogepant.' Table 1 sets the pivotal animal findings (telcagepant: 3M rat <3x ALT/AST, no liver histopathology, 15x margin; 6M rat and 9M NHP no liver signal at 7x; MK-3207: 6M rat none at 25x, 9M NHP none at 4x) beside the clinical findings (telcagepant ALT >3x ULN in 3.2% at 280 mg BID, two symptomatic hepatitis cases >=10-fold, discontinued phase 3; MK-3207 42% (5/12) >500 mg with a Hy's law case, discontinued phase 2). Fields: subjects patients; comparison_stated true; epub_year 2020; print_year 2020; registry_date 2014-09-08 (NCT00797667); model_filed null (telcagepant never filed); product_in_model true; magnitude direction_only; source_calls_it null (states the silence, does not editorialise); population Unselected. This answers the caller's safety question: contra is supportable from a primary peer-reviewed source with a Merck co-author.

safety same 2020 (in vitro + DILIsym) in the same Smith 2020 paper, which predates Woodhead 2022: 'To our knowledge, this study is the first published example of DILIsym predicting liver safety of a dosing regimen before the clinical trial was conducted.' The dedicated hepatic-safety trial (516 healthy adults, 100 mg 2-days-on/2-off, 8 weeks) is the comparison; Woodhead 2022 then extends to rimegepant/zavegepant/atogepant without a status change.

dose: a preclinical (rhesus) dose comparison exists in Smith 2020 Methods: clinically effective doses of telcagepant, MK-3207 and ubrogepant were projected from rhesus CIDV corrected for human potency and protein binding, and 'Clinically effective doses were later confirmed in initial clinical trials for all 3 compounds.' Methods-level, no numbers; Table 1 footnote b records MK-3207's 'original projected daily dose was 80 mg' against 200 mg efficacious (2.5x). Use it if the human-CIDV model is ruled out as non-preclinical.

engagement: Moore 2020 (10.1124/jpet.119.261065; JPET 373(1):160, epub 2020-01-28) as the entry carrying the stated rhesus-vs-human CIDV comparison (3.2 vs 2.6 nM, within_2x, comparison_stated true, subjects healthy_volunteers, product_in_model true).
rule_questions: Does a self-juxtaposition of two primary sources (comparison_stated=false) satisfy rule 1 for `same`? The v2 field implies it may; the checker brief's failure list implies it does not. Engagement 2010 hinges on this; Moore 2020 resolves it either way.

Is a healthy-volunteer human PD model (human capsaicin dermal blood flow, Sinclair 2010 / Li 2015) a 'preclinical model' for this atlas? The dose `same` at 2015 rests on it; the rhesus-only version would rest on Smith 2020's methods statement.

Do in vitro hepatotoxicity assays plus DILIsym (in silico QST) count as a preclinical model? The FDA review names the package as submitted nonclinical data, so it meets 'the model the class relied on', but it is not an animal model. Safety 2019/2020/2022 hinge on this.

When the class switched liver-safety model (rat/monkey toxicology -> in vitro + QST) and the old model is contradicted while the new one matches, both published in the same 2020 paper, does `contra` on the superseded model override `same` on the replacement? 'Contra overrides every matched status' and 'best model = the one relied on' pull in opposite directions.

Dose: one within-2x hit (telcagepant, 300 mg) and one 2.5-10x miss (MK-3207: 20 mg predicted / 80 mg projected vs 200 mg efficacious) in the same source. Does a single miss make `contra` for the cell, or does the source's own 'reasonable correlation' (not re-verified; full text unreachable) keep `same`?
